title: ABL transactions are BLOCK-scoped (DO TRANSACTION), not begin/commit — the batch commits atomically; maps to a single @Transactional boundary
sourceContent:
/* post-batch.p - post every order in a batch atomically */
DEFINE INPUT PARAMETER piBatch AS INTEGER NO-UNDO.

DO TRANSACTION:
    FOR EACH Order WHERE Order.BatchId = piBatch EXCLUSIVE-LOCK:
        Order.Status = "POSTED".
        RUN update-ledger.p (INPUT Order.OrderNum, INPUT Order.Total).
    END.
END.  /* the WHOLE batch commits or rolls back together */
notes: The DO TRANSACTION block bounds the transaction: every Order.Status update AND the update-ledger.p side effects commit or roll back together (per-batch granularity). The Java target is a single @Transactional method over the batch — NOT per-record. An UNDO would reverse the whole block. Getting the granularity wrong (per-record @Transactional) breaks the atomicity guarantee.
